title: When a Lottery Ticket Is Worth More Than It Costs

beats.text: There was a lottery where buying tickets made you money.
In Michigan, a game called Winfall had a strange rule. If the jackpot passed five million dollars and nobody won it, the money rolled down to the smaller prizes.
Suddenly, matching just a few numbers paid far more than usual.
A retired shopkeeper named Jerry Selbee did the maths in minutes. On those weeks, the average ticket was worth more than it cost.
So he bought thousands. Over nine years, he and his wife Marge won almost twenty-seven million dollars in prizes.
Legally. They didn't cheat the lottery. They read the rules.
Every roll-down week, the maths said the same thing.
